findings.problem: JobWorkflow has no enum-based state machine; any combination of status, is_validated, is_sent is structurally allowed including invalid ones like status="sent" with is_validated=false
findings.failure_mode: callers construct and mutate JobWorkflow fields independently, producing states that should never exist (e.g. an unvalidated job marked sent, or a sent job that is not actually sent according to its boolean flag)
findings.fix: Replace the struct fields with a single JobState enum (e.g. Pending, Validated, Sent) that encodes valid transitions. Constructors and transitions return JobState directly; callers cannot assemble illegal combinations.

findings.problem: status is pub String, allowing arbitrary text values ("", "SENT", "pending", "", any runtime string) instead of a closed set of domain states
findings.failure_mode: callers pass typos, wrong casing, or non-domain strings; downstream match or comparison logic silently misbehaves or panics; no compile-time enforcement of valid statuses
findings.fix: Replace `pub status: String` with `pub status: JobStatus` where JobStatus is an enum with explicit variants (Pending, Validated, Sent). Remove the separate is_sent and is_validated booleans once the enum owns the state.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are independent lifecycle booleans that can contradict each other (e.g. is_validated=false, is_sent=true) and cannot express ordering (validated must precede sent)
findings.failure_mode: callers set booleans in any order or skip steps entirely; the struct admits logically impossible states with no compile-time guard; transitions are not enforced
findings.fix: Encode lifecycle in a single enum typestate (Pending -> Validated -> Sent) so each variant owns the boolean information it needs and invalid transitions are impossible at the type level.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is decoupled from the lifecycle booleans; a job can have sent_at_epoch_ms=Some(…) with is_sent=false, or is_sent=true with sent_at_epoch_ms=None
findings.failure_mode: callers produce inconsistent state where sent-time data exists without the sent flag or vice versa; logic reading sent_at_epoch_ms cannot trust is_sent and vice versa
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms into the Sent variant of the typestate enum: `Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }`. This makes illegal combinations unrepresentable at compile time.

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive that carries no domain invariants (format, length, uniqueness); any string is accepted including empty, whitespace, or malformed identifiers
findings.failure_mode: callers pass empty strings, unbounded input, or malformed IDs; no validation at construction; accidental mixing of ID types across domains
findings.fix: Replace with `pub id: JobId` where JobId is a newtype wrapping a validated representation (e.g. `struct JobId(String)` with a smart constructor that returns Result<JobId, ParseError>). Parse hostile input once at the shell boundary.

findings.problem: Raw primitives (String, bool, Option<u64>) cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors; callers can construct invalid domain states directly from untrusted data
findings.failure_mode: external input (JSON deserialization, API payloads, file data) populates JobWorkflow fields with invalid values; there is no single parse point that enforces invariants before core logic sees the data
findings.fix: Define JobWorkflow (or a new JobDomain type) with private fields and a single fallible constructor: `fn try_from(id: &str, status: &str, validated: bool) -> Result<Self, JobError>`. The constructor parses and validates once, producing a trusted domain value. The core logic consumes only trusted types.

findings.problem: mark_sent accepts any JobWorkflow regardless of its current state and overwrites status to "sent" without checking that is_validated=true or any precondition; it also ignores sent_at_epoch_ms
findings.failure_mode: callers can mark any job as sent without validation; the function silently accepts invalid preconditions and produces a sent-but-not-validated job
findings.fix: Change the function signature to accept a validated-specific state: `fn mark_sent(state: ValidatedState) -> SentState`. Each transition type takes the prior state and returns the next state, encoding preconditions in the type system.

residual_risk: Static review only; no commands executed. The code structurally permits all illegal state combinations through independent primitive fields. No typestate enum, no parse boundary, no smart constructors, and no precondition enforcement on transitions. A full repair would require replacing the entire struct with an enum-based typestate machine, newtyped IDs, fallible constructors, and transition functions with typed inputs/outputs.
